key_insight: The paper shows that sparse autoencoders can become unreliable at scale because meaningful concepts get split across multiple latents or absorbed as arbitrary exceptions. It introduces cross-sample consistency regularization (C$^{2}$R) to keep features more atomic and stable across examples.
problem_solved: It addresses two major failure modes in large sparse autoencoders: feature splitting, where one concept fragments into multiple latents, and feature absorption, where general features swallow irregular exceptions and lose interpretability.
method: Adds a cross-sample consistency regularization term to encourage the same concept to be represented consistently across different inputs.
Penalizes unstable latent assignments so features remain more atomic and less sensitive to sample-specific quirks.
Improves SAE training at large dictionary sizes to reduce fragmentation and exception absorption.
impact: For practitioners using SAEs to interpret LLMs, this can make learned features more trustworthy, readable, and easier to analyze. It is especially important when scaling interpretability methods to larger and more realistic models.

paper_title: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
paper_authors: Haoran Jin, Xiting Wang, Shijie Ren, Hong Xie, Defu Lian
